rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments completed, there is no evidence to guide exploitation; the priority is establishing a clear, interpretable baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest viable configuration: a single modality, a single profile, and the most straightforward linear encoder (PCA). It carries minimal implementation risk and isolates the core classification task without confounding from fusion, aggregation, or learned encoders. This baseline performance will serve as the reference floor against which we can measure the incremental contribution of each design axis (profile setting, encoder choice, image modality, aggregation, fusion) in subsequent experiments. Starting at the simplest corner of the design space allows each follow-up to change one dimension at a time, maximizing the information gained per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: Only one experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is complete, yielding ~48.5% accuracy and ~46.4% F1, establishing a weak RNA-only baseline. The largest unresolved design question is whether adding image information provides complementary signal. Question tested: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the minimal-change extension of config_001—identical RNA encoder and profile setting, with only the addition of a ResNet50 image branch and simple concat fusion. This isolates the effect of the image modality. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) model_setting (unimodal vs. multimodal) is the highest-level design decision; resolving it can eliminate or prioritize ~36 of the remaining 50 configs. (2) It is a clean A/B comparison to config_001, changing only the addition of image, so any performance difference can be attributed to the image branch. (3) If multimodal significantly outperforms RNA-only, it justifies investing remaining budget in multimodal variants (better encoders, aggregation, fusion). If it does not, the search can focus on improving the RNA representation (scvi, scgpt) or profile/aggregation strategies within the unimodal space, avoiding wasted experiments on a modality that adds no value.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, PCA, single) scored 0.485 acc and config_016 (multimodal, PCA+ResNet50, concat, single) scored 0.527 acc, showing a ~4.2% gain from adding the image modality. However, we lack the image-only baseline, so we cannot determine whether the multimodal gain reflects genuine cross-modal synergy or simply that the image carries stronger independent signal than RNA. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, ResNet50) completes the {RNA, Image, Both} comparison triangle under identical profile and encoder conditions, isolating the image's standalone contribution. Why this is the best next step: Without this baseline, we cannot judge whether the multimodal result is truly additive/synergistic or whether a simpler image-only model would suffice. This single clean comparison (removing only the RNA branch from config_016) reduces the most critical uncertainty before investing further experiments in more complex multimodal variants (multiprofile, alternative encoders, weighted fusion). It is the highest-information experiment per unit budget at this stage.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc / 0.510 F1, a clear ~4-point gain over RNA-only (config_001: 0.485/0.464), confirming that multimodal fusion with these encoders is beneficial. Image alone (config_010: 0.208) is weak, so the gain comes from complementary information. Uncertainty: We have only tested concat fusion; weighted fusion is untested and could redistribute modality contributions more effectively (especially given the large performance gap between RNA and image). This experiment (config_017) changes exactly one variable—fusion from concat to weighted—while holding model setting, profile setting, RNA encoder, and image encoder identical to config_016. This clean A/B comparison isolates the effect of fusion strategy. If weighted outperforms concat, it identifies a low-cost improvement to carry forward into all future multimodal experiments (multiprofile, alternative encoders). If they are comparable, we can deprioritize fusion and redirect budget toward the larger unexplored dimensions (multiprofile, scvi/scgpt encoders, ViT image encoder). Under a limited budget, this single-variable test maximizes information per experiment.

Evidence: Our best result so far is config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) at 52.7% accuracy, showing a modest ~4pp gain over RNA-only (48.5%) and a negligible difference between concat and weighted fusion. The single most important unexplored design dimension is profile setting (single vs. multi), which has not been tested in any completed experiment. Question: config_018 is a clean single-variable extension of config_016—identical model setting, RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion—changing only the profile setting from single to multi (necessitating avgpool aggregation). This directly tests whether multiprofile + avgpool aggregation improves upon the current best configuration. Why best next experiment: If multiprofile helps, it opens a high-value direction across many downstream configs (different encoders, fusion methods, aggregation strategies). If it does not help, we can efficiently prune the entire multiprofile branch and focus remaining budget on RNA encoder or image encoder choices within singleprofile. This one experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about a major architectural axis while building directly on our strongest evidence.

The strongest result so far is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc, a large jump over the single-profile multimodal baseline (config_016, 0.527). However, this comparison conflates three changes: adding a second modality (already tested), switching to multiprofile, and introducing avgpool aggregation. The critical open question is whether the multiprofile+avgpool benefit is inherent to the RNA representation or requires the multimodal interaction. config_002 (RNA-only, multiprofile, PCA n2000, avgpool) is a clean single-variable extension of config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile) that isolates the multiprofile/aggregation effect on the RNA side alone. If RNA multiprofile alone yields a substantial gain (e.g., >0.55), the benefit is in the RNA profile representation and we should prioritize multiprofile RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) next. If it stays near 0.485, the gain is synergistic and we should focus on the multimodal aggregation design (e.g., transformer in config_020). This ablation is the highest-information experiment under the budget because it disambiguates the mechanism behind the largest observed effect and directly guides the next 2-3 experiments.

Evidence: The largest performance jump in the study came from switching to multiprofile (config_018: 0.619 vs config_016: 0.527 for multimodal; config_002: 0.591 vs config_001: 0.485 for RNA-only), and the only aggregation tested so far is avgpool. Fusion method (concat vs weighted) showed negligible difference in singleprofile (0.527 vs 0.523), so it is lower priority. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for combining multiple profiles, given that the multiprofile gain is the dominant source of accuracy? This experiment (config_020) changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other parameters at their current best values (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat), cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. Why best next: It is a single-variable extension of the current best configuration, directly tests whether a more expressive aggregation can further exploit the multiprofile signal, and the result will inform whether transformer aggregation is worth exploring across other encoder/fusion combinations under the limited budget.

Evidence: RNA is the dominant signal (image-only acc=0.208; RNA-only multiprofile avgpool=0.591 is close to the best multimodal result of 0.619), and multiprofile+avgpool is the strongest setting so far. However, we have only tested PCA-2000 as the RNA encoder—a linear projection—across all 7 completed experiments. The RNA encoder is the highest-uncertainty, highest-impact design axis remaining. Question: config_005 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_002 (same setting but PCA-2000), isolating whether a learned generative representation (scvi) captures more predictive structure than PCA. Why this is the best use of the next experiment: it directly tests the most consequential unexplored axis (RNA representation quality) without confounding from image modality, fusion, or aggregation changes. If scvi_n200 improves RNA-only performance, we gain a strong prior for deploying it in the multimodal multiprofile setting; if not, PCA remains validated and we can redirect budget toward image encoder or other axes. This maximizes information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: scvi_n200 substantially outperforms PCA n2000 in the RNA-only multi-profile setting (0.650 vs 0.591, config_005 vs config_002), and the best multimodal config so far (config_018: PCA, multi, avgpool, concat, ResNet50) achieves 0.619. Question: Does the scvi_n200 encoder improvement transfer to the multimodal setting? config_030 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200 relative to config_018 (keeping multi-profile, avgpool, concat, ResNet50), cleanly isolating the encoder effect in the multimodal context. Why this is the best next experiment: It directly exploits the strongest single finding (scvi > PCA) in the most promising model architecture, uses a single-variable change to maintain interpretability, and if it succeeds, establishes scvi_n200 as the preferred encoder for further exploration (e.g., with ViT or transformer aggregation). If it fails, it tells us the scvi benefit is specific to RNA-only and the image modality interacts differently with the learned representation.

Evidence: The RNA encoder is the most impactful design axis so far — switching from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in the multiprofile RNA-only setting improved accuracy from 0.591 to 0.650 (+0.06), the largest single-factor gain observed. However, scgpt has not been tested at all, leaving a major uncertainty about whether a third, potentially stronger RNA representation exists. Question: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005 (same settings but scvi_n200), isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly tests the most consequential unexplored axis before committing budget to multimodal or image-encoder variants built on top of it. (2) If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi, it reopens the multimodal search with a stronger RNA backbone; if it underperforms, we can confidently focus remaining budget on scvi-based configurations. (3) It changes only one factor relative to config_005, avoiding the confound of simultaneously altering encoder, modality, or aggregation. This maximizes information gained per experiment under the limited budget.
